note: Upstream Python package at the tag. The compiled extensions (csrc) come from the pinned container's install of the same tag; tools/stage-vllm-overlay.sh layers this tree over that install. vllm/vllm/config/fault_tolerance.py is stored LF-normalized (upstream has CRLF).

local_patches.why: back the CUDA caching allocator with expandable (VMM) segments, set before CUDA is initialized and again in Worker.init_device; only the mapping under an allocator segment changes (VLLM_EXPANDABLE_SEGMENTS=0 keeps the default allocator)
GB10 exposes no NVML memory clock; fall back to 273 GB/s for humming's tuning heuristic
VLLM_HUMMING_BATCH_INVARIANT=1 turns on humming's deterministic MoE kernels without the global batch-invariant mode (which forces CUTLASS W4A4 on W4A16 linears)

when the optional l2pf kernel package (harness/kernels/l2pf) is importable, the FULL CUDA graph gets one extra side-stream node per GEMM that L2-prefetches the first tiles of the next GEMM's weights; the GEMM sites are recorded on the warm-up run before the capture, only model parameters are prefetched, and no kernel on the main stream changes (L2PF=0 turns it off)

the accepted glimmer_fp8_ext G2 tile serves the supported small FP8 GEMMs on GB10 with the stock accumulation order and scale rounding. L2 prefetch records the actual native launch or the stock CUTLASS overload with the same model weight pointer

local_patches.file: vllm/model_executor/layers/mamba/ops/ssd_pinned_configs.py (+ pins in ssd_state_passing.py, ssd_bmm.py, ssd_chunk_scan.py, ssd_chunk_state.py)
local_patches.why: Triton autotune picked different SSD tile configs per boot on GB10, making the same prompt yield one of two token streams; each kernel is pinned to one config (VLLM_MAMBA_SSD_AUTOTUNE=1 restores autotuning)

the attention output gate projection reads the layer input, so for decode-sized batches it is launched before attention and the attention chain (QK-norm, RoPE, KV-cache write, attention) runs beside it on a high-priority side stream; fork, switch and join are graph splitting points, so the gate projection is a compiled piece of its own and the FULL CUDA graph gets a fork and a join; the same kernels run on the same inputs, unquantized (cuBLAS) gate projections keep the stock order (VLLM_MUSE_GLIMMER_GATE_STREAM=0 turns it off)
skip the MTP drafter when every request in the batch has max_tokens == 1: its drafts are never verified, and the drafter's pass over the prompt delayed the sampled token (the timed prefill)

NVFP4 W4A16 weights much larger than L2 (MLP gate_up and down) run calls of 128 rows or more through harness/kernels/marlinw when it is built (the Marlin kernel body on the same work slices as ops.marlin_gemm, handed out column-major); a layer without it runs prompt-sized calls as ops.marlin_gemm on column slices of a slice-major copy of the same prepared weight where both schedules compute every tile whole-K with the same config, else the single call; each path is admitted per layer by a load-time bitwise comparison with the single call

in-process engine core for the single-request engine loop: InprocClient pauses automatic garbage collection while the engine has work and drains a finished request's queued batch on abort (no busy loop does it in this mode); hostfast.py also restricts the process to the highest-capacity CPU cores when the cores differ, failing soft (VLLM_HOSTFAST_GC=0 and VLLM_HOSTFAST_PIN=0 switch each off)

one-token FP8 w8a8 GEMMs (decode) run through musefp8, a hand-written mma.sync m16n8k32 e4m3 GEMV that issues the same instruction chain in the same k order as cutlass_scaled_mm's SM120 M16 kernel and the same ScaledEpilogue (bf16_rn(scale_a * fp32(scale_b * acc))), reading a fragment-ordered copy of each weight (registered as a layer buffer) with L2 evict-first loads; every layer is admitted only after a load-time bitwise comparison with cutlass_scaled_mm; other row counts keep glimmer_fp8 / cutlass; the op is an l2pf site (MUSEFP8=0 disables, MUSEFP8_L2PF=0 drops it from the prefetch chain). Compressed one-row QKV sites (4608x6656) and compressed output sites (6656x4096) that follow attention stay in the chain for matching but get no prefetch of their own; the capture log line counts them. When harness/kernels/muserans is built, each FP8 weight is instead stored as an exponent-pair rANS stream with raw sign|mantissa nibbles (lossless, ~0.84 of the bytes on this checkpoint) and decoded inside the same GEMV right before the same mma.sync chain, so the output bits are unchanged and the decode step reads fewer bytes; admitted per layer by the same bitwise check (MUSERANS=0 keeps the uncompressed copy) Imported from zereraz's Yukon submission cdefbb34-137b-48d9-9179-db4b540fbf57 (evaluation source 56791c43d807320c42d93b023678800489f6500c).

Uses zereraz's published 6-bit palette implementation from cdefbb34 / 56791c43 for one-row NVFP4 decode after the per-layer bitwise admission check. The existing BF16 and FP8 SwiGLU prefill and narrow down operation signatures preserve their arguments.

The single-device 512-row static FP8 MLP gate/up dispatches to harness/kernels/muse_fp8_swiglu when its down projection accepts static FP8. Alternating checkpoint output columns brings the BF16 gate and up values into one CUTLASS thread fragment. The arithmetic uses the G2 scaled-MM multiply order and the existing BF16 SiLU lookup before packing the down-scale E4M3 byte. The input uses its original FP8 quantizer before shape dispatch.

Carries only ArthurOstapenko's prompt query normalization and RoPE launcher and installation hook from Yukon submission fa040f4a-ca7e-42dd-8f50-8f1aadfc8d9b (ranked aa3a2e54b58675aa76f633bd31a3d07b0e4d41ab), first published in e7600084-0e57-465b-8c3c-1df33c51dd94. Before replacing a matching compiled kernel, the launcher compares output bits against the actual stock compiler kernel. The default minimum batch size is 128 tokens.

The unquantized BF16 Muse Glimmer QKV and output gate on one CUDA device admit the one-row lane-striped GEMV only after a complete lossless weight check and per-layer bitwise cuBLAS comparisons. It keeps the original lane accumulation and warp fold. Larger row counts, bias and other weights retain the stock linear method. The original weights remain the fallback and the L2 site reads only the registered compact buffer. MUSE_BF16_LANE=0 selects the original paths.

Keep the full compiled backbone and specialize only the final two independent-row NVFP4 projection launches inside the logits-only prefill capture. Retain both operator output shapes and the ordered K partition for the sampled tile. Full-output consumers use the original projection launches.

The 512-row NVFP4 attention projections (qkv 4608x6656, output gate 4096x6656, o 6656x4096) run the stock ops.marlin_gemm partition on the narrow marlinw_down kernel (same device code, two blocks per SM, one block per 128-column half of each stock slice, unsplit tiles column-major, cut slices longest first). Every slice keeps its chunk, K range, slice_idx and slice_count, so each output element keeps its K16 MMA chains, FP32 split-K order and BF16 epilogue. A layer is admitted only after a bitwise comparison with the single ops.marlin_gemm call on its own weights; others, decode and every other row count keep the stock call. MARLIN_NARROW_ATTN=0 selects the original path.

On a unified-memory GPU the rate a one-row NVFP4 GEMV reaches is a property of the physical memory under its weight and differs by several percent between allocations of the same bytes. After the load, every group of same-shaped decode weights is timed with the tiled decode GEMV on its own buffers and on spare buffers of the same size; weights on slow buffers are copied to faster spares and compared bitwise before the buffer is exchanged. No kernel, operand value or prompt-sized weight changes. Any error or a short host leaves the loader's placement. MUSE_DECODE_PLACEMENT=0 disables the step.

The same load-time placement for the prompt-sized NVFP4 MLP weights: the production 512-row fused gate/up and down kernels are timed on every prefill weight and on spare buffers of the same size (the same weight in two allocations runs these kernels 11-17% apart on GB10, because whether a weight tile stays in L2 between its reads depends on the physical pages under it), and weights on slow buffers are copied to faster spares, compared bitwise and exchanged before anything is compiled or captured. MUSE_PREFILL_PLACEMENT=0 disables the step.

local_patches.file: harness/kernels/l2pf/py/sites.py (outside the vLLM subtree; recorded here for provenance)
local_patches.why: L2 prefetch heads ahead of the MLP GEMMs (weights above MAX_WEIGHT): a 2.25 MiB head ahead of gate_up (after a norm) and a 0.5 MiB head ahead of down (after the activation), scales sharing the budget, plus a re-entrancy guard so only the outermost call of a nested wrapped entry point is a site. Taken from ArthurOstapenko's published submission e8fa7600-36f4-49a5-9c70-4190970fa897 (branch commit af81404); our compressed-FP8 prefetch skip (_RANS_SKIP_PREFETCH) is kept. Prefetch only reads weight bytes into L2 on a side stream; no value changes. L2PF_MLP=0 disables the heads.

Prompt-sized (M > 16) FP8 w8a8 GEMMs of the attention projections and FP8 down projections run through CUTLASS 4.5 SM120 kernels whose tile shape and pipeline depth suit 512 rows on GB10, instead of vLLM's sm120 kernel (128x128x128 tile, 2 stages). They use the same CUTLASS SM120 mainloop (SM120_16x8x32_TN e4m3 MMA, one fp32 accumulator per element, k32 MMA blocks in k order, no split-K or stream-K) and the same ScaledEpilogue arithmetic bf16_rn(scale_a * fp32_rn(scale_b * acc)), so each output element is computed by the same instruction chain in the same order. Each layer is admitted at load only after a bitwise comparison with ops.cutlass_scaled_mm on its own weight (512/300/33 rows, three activation patterns); the first eager call per weight is also compared with the stock op on its real activation and logged. MUSE_FP8_PREFILL=0 disables it.

512-row FP8 w8a8 GEMMs of the attention qkv (4608x6656) and output-gate (4096x6656) projections run on fp8ws, taken from SP5D's published Yukon submission 98c1361e-289f-45a3-8471-5df0259bd3b2 (branch commit b520efe): a persistent 8-warp mma.sync kind::f8f6f4 m16n8k32 GEMM fed by 2-D TMA straight from the loaded weight (no repack). Kernel source and build script unchanged; SHAPES cut to these two shapes, where it beat stock CUTLASS in sustained capped timing on GB10, and the rival's load-time timing gate replaced by that fixed routing (o_proj stays on stock CUTLASS, down on muse_fp8_prefill, FP8 gate/up on muse_fp8_swiglu). Each output element is one ascending-K MMA chain from +0 with the ScaledEpilogue arithmetic, as in CUTLASS; each shape is admitted only after a bitwise comparison with ops.cutlass_scaled_mm on the live, a random and a bit-pattern activation (SP5D's check). FP8WS=0 disables it.

Decode host path from SP5D's published Yukon submission 98c1361e-289f-45a3-8471-5df0259bd3b2 (branch commit b520efe), three pieces only: constant one-request sampling metadata tensors made once (cu_num_logits, expanded_local_pos; only read downstream) instead of an arange and a zeros launch per step; no eager attention-metadata build for steps that replay a FULL CUDA graph (the replay reads the persistent input, block-table and slot-mapping buffers, which are still filled; FlashAttention-2 metadata building writes no persistent buffer; not used with a speculator); and for a one-request decode step with one sampled token, no copy-back of num_sampled_tokens (the output is [[token]], as the general path gives). SP5D's spin wait on the output event, the max_kv_len decode graphs, the canonical block-pool head and its engine-core scheduling changes are not taken.

The boot prefill graph (ArthurOstapenko's whole-forward prefill graph, Yukon submission c1e4b913) also captures the text embedding of the prompt's token ids (the same eager embed_input_ids of the language model, which is what the multimodal embedding path returns for a prompt without media), and a text-only one-request prefill that the graph can replay passes its token-id buffer instead of an eagerly computed embedding; if the replay is refused, the eager embedding is computed then. Taken from SP5D's published Yukon submission 98c1361e-289f-45a3-8471-5df0259bd3b2 (branch commit b520efe), prefill graph only: its embedding inside the decode graphs and its compile-partition change are not taken.

The FlashInfer autotune pass of kernel_warmup is skipped (SP5D's published Yukon submission 98c1361e-289f-45a3-8471-5df0259bd3b2, branch commit b520efe; its extra empty_cache is not taken). On this model the pass tunes no FlashInfer op (it saves 0 configs) and only repeats a max-size dummy forward, about 50 s of boot; Inductor's kernel configs were all chosen during compilation, before it, so no kernel choice changes. Boot time only.

512-row NVFP4 gate/up (paired SwiGLU) and down projections run on 128-row tiles that dequantize each weight fragment once for twice the rows, taken unchanged from e-man07's published Yukon submission a53190a4-8004-4a8b-b026-0cf0964f8af3 (branch commit eb2d466): libmarlinw_swiglu2 is used for a layer only after a bitwise comparison with the 64-row kernel on its own weight (MARLINW_SWIGLU2=0 disables); marlinw_down128 keeps marlinw_down's per-element MMA chains, K cuts and fp32 fold and is admitted per layer by the 512-row prompt check (MARLIN_DOWN128=0 disables). Muse Glimmer addition: the load-time prefill weight placement times the kernel each group will run (the 128-row kernels when every layer of the group was admitted) and a moved weight keeps its admission (both routes are keyed by the weight's address).

Bit-exact lossless decode and prefill stack over c47a794: (1) continuous per-warp FP8 rANS streams without 4-byte step padding in muserans (117 layers); (2) persistent cp.async NS=4 high-byte rANS BF16 decode GEMV in muse_bf16_lane (12 layers, -54.7 MB/tok) with compressed BF16 QKV L2-prefetch skip in l2pf; (3) compact 704-byte rANS block-scale headers and GPU Pass-1/Pass-2 encoder in decode6 (45 gate/up + 40 down layers); (4) Fast Pool v2 weight placement in decode_placement.py (posix_fadvise(DONTNEED) shard cache drop, read-only L2 eviction flush, non-recycling slow-buffer hold across groups, 2.5x surplus with 12 lm_head spares, plus muserans FP8 MLP and muse_fp8_prefill FP8 down placement); (5) single highest-capacity L3 cluster pinning and pure-C SCHED_IDLE 1 ms deep-idle prevention tickler in hostfast.py/l2pf.cu; (6) zero-spill 128x128-tile NVFP4 attention QKV prefill in marlinw_down128 (18 layers) plus cached scratch buffers in marlinw_down128/marlinw_attn/marlinw_down; (7) CUTLASS 128x192 FP8 o_proj prefill in muse_fp8_prefill (42 layers); and (8) prefill post_attn norm glue extension in muse_glimmer_norm_glue.py. Every kernel is admitted only after per-layer bitwise equality checks.

A one-row greedy decode step without logprobs, penalties, bias or grammar takes its token from lmpost, taken from SP5D's published Yukon submission 98c1361e-289f-45a3-8471-5df0259bd3b2 (branch commit b520efe): the lm_head output goes through a 64K-entry BF16 table of this model's compute_logits chain (x * output_multiplier, then cap * tanh(x / cap), built by the same torch ops on every BF16 value) fused with a one-pass argmax whose ties go to the lowest index, the stock greedy sampler's rule; the sampling row is taken as a slice. Its in-place softcap hook for compute_logits is not taken, and the token is written to a freshly allocated tensor instead of two alternating persistent ones. LMPOST=0 disables it.

This stack starts from zereraz's published Yukon submission 8810a7b7-086b-48fa-a5aa-c6f938ce2421 (branch commit 84bd233, itself built on our accepted 4203115e): every change of that commit (the entry above that begins 'Bit-exact lossless decode and prefill stack over c47a794' is zereraz's) is taken unchanged, including its weight placement, host pinning and idle tickler. Added on top by the Muse Glimmer team: the lmpost decode argmax (from SP5D 98c1361e), the 512-row route log lines, and the reply-first settle plus two-stage prefill output wait in the resident path.

local_patches.file: vllm/model_executor/kernels/linear/nvfp4/marlin.py; harness/kernels/marlinw (csrc/marlinw_tma.cu new, py/swiglu.py, build.sh), harness/kernels/marlinw_down128 (marlinw_down128.py, build.sh)
local_patches.why: 512-row NVFP4 gate/up (paired SwiGLU) and down projections: e-man07's 128-row tiles (published Yukon submission a53190a4-8004-4a8b-b026-0cf0964f8af3, branch commit eb2d466) with their operands copied to shared memory by TMA bulk tensor copies that one thread per CTA starts, instead of cp.async issued by every MMA warp (activations as a 128 B x 128-row box with SWIZZLE_128B, which is the same xor layout; codes and scales as plain boxes; mbarrier complete_tx handoff; TMA mechanics as in SP5D's fp8ws, published Yukon submission 98c1361e-289f-45a3-8471-5df0259bd3b2), and with the fe2m1 -> bf16 placement of each 8 codes written as mask, multiply, mask (the same four registers bit for bit). Down projection: the 16 tiles left after four full waves are split in K into three full 128x128 pieces (120/96/96 k-tiles) instead of 48 row-split CTAs; a later piece continues from the accumulator registers its predecessor stored (flag hand-over in the work list, reset by the kernel), so every MMA chain is the whole tile's chain; the stock K-cut hook runs between loop segments instead of as predicated code in every k-tile. Gate/up epilogue: SiLU is evaluated with the instruction sequence that fills e-man07's 64K-entry table instead of read from it; swiglu_prepare compares both for all 65536 BF16 patterns (FP32 bit for bit) and refuses the library on any difference. Tiles, register layouts, per-element MMA chains, K cuts, fp32 fold and both epilogues are otherwise e-man07's. libmarlinw_swiglu3 is used for a layer only after a bitwise comparison with the 64-row kernel on its own weight (MARLINW_SWIGLU3=0 disables; fallback libmarlinw_swiglu2, then the 64-row kernel), libmarlinw_down128t only after the 512-row prompt check against the single stock call (MARLIN_DOWN128_TMA=0 disables; fallback libmarlinw_down128); the load-time prefill weight placement times the kernel each group will run and a moved weight keeps its admission; one log line reports how many layers run the TMA-fed kernels.

Wave-8 bit-exact prefill and decode optimizations over 9daf69d2-f9f2-45b6-b747-0b0d69573a2c (kaankolcu, itself built on zereraz's 8810a7b7-086b-48fa-a5aa-c6f938ce2421 and ea4258c3-25d8-45ad-9385-71607d666636): (1) PG=4 full column-group L2 locality in marlinw_down128.tma_work_lists (39 NVFP4 down prefill layers read weights once per column instead of twice; D128_TMA_PG=2 restores PG=2); (2) TMA-fed 128-row FP8-output paired SwiGLU kernel (libmarlinw_swiglu3_fp8.so from marlinw_tma.cu -DMARLINW_TMA_FP8) with direct SiLU and cvt.rn.satfinite.e4m3x2.f32 for the 5 NVFP4-gate_up + FP8-down prefill layers, admitted per layer by bitwise comparison with 64-row libmarlinw_swiglu_fp8 (MARLINW_SWIGLU3_FP8=0 disables), with moved() hook forwarding in swiglu.py; (3) TMA-fed 128x128 PG=4 NVFP4 QKV (4608x6656, 18 layers, 3 exact waves) prefill via marlinw_tma.cu (MARLIN_ATTN_TMA=0 disables); (4) CUTLASS SM120 FP8 prefill k=128 tiles Cfg2 (128x192x128 for down) and Cfg3 (128x96x128 for o_proj and qkv, routed ahead of fp8ws in glimmer_fp8.py while keeping gate on fp8ws), from spariev's published Yukon submissions f4ad6eeb-4173-4f4a-8a99-d63014350827 / 262ee4f1-5e65-47ab-8d1a-9b106df1feaa (branch commits 787513e / 24bd994), plus per-device cached 1 MiB scratch buffer outside graph capture; (5) 4-stage TMA super-block rANS block scales in decode6 (gemv6_tma4.cu) covering all 45 gate_up, 40 down, and lm_head NVFP4 decode layers via hardware cp.async.bulk (4.033 / 3.909 bits/scale, admitted per layer by bitwise check; MUSE_TMA4=0 disables); (6) decode_placement.py: SURPLUS=3.5 / LM_HEAD_SPARES=16 with selective slow-only hold (releasing faster-than-median unused spares between decode groups and clearing before prefill), timing fp8_down with Cfg2, and adding 7x254 MiB paired_fp8_swiglu_weight prefill placement (MUSE_PREFILL_FP8_SWIGLU=0 disables). Every kernel preserves exact stock accumulation order and passes per-layer bitwise admission.

Wave-9 bit-exact decode and reliability optimizations over Wave-8 (d45f9a81-2b5e-402b-8632-63ed65981e77): (1) 2 MiB in-kernel GMMU address-translation prefetch (prefetch.global.L2 in block 0) in muserans (117 FP8 layers, MUSERANS_TLB_PREFETCH=2048, idea from ArthurOstapenko's published submission 75967574-35df-4ee1-b261-e2a38e632bd1) and in muse_bf16_lane (12 BF16 rANS layers, MUSE_BF16_TLB_PREFETCH=2048) plus even 48-SM virtual-warp distribution in muse_bf16_lane (idea from SP5D's 418a64bd-17d2-4d8d-95c7-34438edb7253); (2) side-stream 2 MiB GMMU TLB pre-warming in l2pf/py/sites.py (appending one 128 B/2 MiB strided bulk-prefetch descriptor to each of the 184 existing assisted GEMM sites with zero additional CUDA graph nodes; L2PF_TLB=0 disables); (3) stage-interleaved 48-CTA stream-K NVFP4 down layout (MUSE_DOWN_ILV=1, default) in decode6 TMA4 (chunk 48*s + b, preserving exact (rows, 32) scale shape, making all 48 SMs read 384 KiB contiguous DRAM per stage and letting l2pf's 512 KiB head warm all 48 SMs' stage 0, admitted per layer by bitwise check), plus compile-time M=1 specialization in if constexpr (scale6) (SP5D 418a64bd) eliminating all 32 B stack spills across libmuse_marlin6.so (STACK:0 LOCAL:0); (4) M == 1 side-stream attention overlap for the 6 BF16 output_gate_proj layers served by deterministic muse_bf16_lane (restricted strictly to M == 1 when muse_bf16_lane_weight is admitted so M > 1 cuBLAS never overlaps; VLLM_MUSE_GLIMMER_GATE_STREAM_BF16=0 disables); (5) VLLM_MUSE_GLIMMER_PROMPT_GLUE_MIN_TOKENS default lowered from 128 to 1 in muse_glimmer_glue.py (SP5D 418a64bd) removing 64-bit divisions on decode QK-norm + RoPE; (6) decode_placement.py: timing NVFP4 weights with decode_linear6 (TMA4), uniform min_blob timing with host backup in _place_muserans_group (SP5D 418a64bd) to remove compression-ratio confounding, descending byte ordering, and non-starving rejected_hold fallback; (7) two __syncthreads() barriers around the K-cut accumulator scratch store in marlinw_tma.cu (ArthurOstapenko 75967574) closing a concurrent-memory-traffic race with zero arithmetic change.

Wave-10 bit-exact prefill, decode, and placement optimizations over Wave-9 (fe24a871-859b-4094-9826-e91a0bde1c29) and current leader SP5D 4b361357-40d5-4d00-a8e3-16e57aae4ea2: (1) one-pass fused Q/K RMSNorm + query pre-scale + NEOX RoPE CUDA kernel (harness/kernels/muse_qk_glue, custom op vllm::muse_glimmer_qk_norm_rope in muse_glimmer.py, 20-30 regs, 0 spills, load-time verified, VLLM_MUSE_GLIMMER_QK_FUSED=0 kill switch) covering all 52 layers (39 RoPE + 13 NoPE) on both M=512 prefill and M=1 decode (inspired by ArthurOstapenko a9002906-868e-4c76-a654-1eb9145221ba's prompt-only qk_glue, generalized here as a direct torch.compile/CUDA-graph custom op for both prefill and M=1 decode using warp-shuffle NEOX pairing); (2) 32-block (16 warps/block) attention output_gate GEMV in muserans (28 FP8 layers, MUSERANS_GATE_32_BLOCKS=0 disables, idea from ArthurOstapenko a9002906) and in muse_bf16_lane (6 BF16 layers, MUSE_BF16_GATE_32_BLOCKS=0 disables), leaving 16 free SMs for side-stream split-KV flash attention; (3) merged proven prefill/zero-spill/host fast paths from promoted leader SP5D 4b361357-40d5-4d00-a8e3-16e57aae4ea2: -DMARLINW_ONE_SLICE zero-spill libmarlinw_attn.so (REG:254 STACK:0), compile-time M=1 zero-spill libmuse_marlin.so, muse_final_slab dead zeroing removal and scratch reuse, muse_fp8_swiglu capture-guarded scratch caching, parallel harness/kernels/build.sh, and resident.py/backends.py host fast paths; (4) upgraded decode_placement.py combining SP5D 4b361357's cross-phase _SLOW_HOLD quarantine, 25% incremental _ensure_spares_room, HOST_HEADROOM_BYTES=16 GiB, PREFILL_SURPLUS=2.0, col_major stride preservation, and total-bytes group sort with Wave-9's decode_linear6 TMA4/TMA4-ILV + uniform min_blob timing and new 8-group attention placement (MUSE_PLACE_ATTN=1 default: 12 BF16 rANS + 98 FP8 rANS + 46 NVFP4 attention weights = 13 decode groups total).

Wave-11 bit-exact decode, prefill, cache-policy, and full-RAM physical placement optimizations over our promoted Wave-10 leader 62141de3-7688-4675-83f4-5d6722ef6e43 (bb95a9f): (1) pure 8-bit exponent rANS + sign-packed mantissa byte layout and transposed uint4 (LDS.128) shared-memory activation loads in muse_bf16_lane/lane.cu (471.5 -> 464.9 MB across 12 BF16 layers, -6.52 MB/tok, REG:56 STACK:0, verified bitwise per layer against F.linear); (2) coordinated L2 cache eviction policies across SM121a: L2::evict_last on cp.async.bulk.prefetch.L2 in l2pf.cu paired with MUSE_B_EVICT_FIRST (locally materialized createpolicy L2::evict_first + L2::256B in cp_async4_stream, 0 odd-UR descriptors, STACK:0) in decode6/gemv6_tma4.cu, plus L2::evict_last(tmA) / L2::evict_first(tmB/tmS) and warp-aggregated empty_bar arrival in marlinw_tma.cu and L2::evict_last(tmA) / L2::evict_first(tmB) in fp8ws.cu (with FP8 qkv 4608x6656 routed to L2-hint fp8ws by setting MUSE_FP8_PREFILL_QKV default to 0);
